1.note: Amos is speaking of the people of Israel as if they were the **sons** of their ancestor Israel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [against you Israelites]

Here, **all of the family** represents all of the descendants of those who were captive in Egypt. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all of you descendants of those]

Amos first refers to **Yahweh** and then he uses the first person **I** to describe what Yahweh had done. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the second person throughout this verse as in the UST.

2.note: The implication is that when Yahweh says that he has **known** Israel, he means that he chose this people to belong to him in a special covenant relationship. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Only you have I chosen to be in a covenant relationship with me]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the nations or people groups that live on the earth. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people groups that live on the earth]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquities**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [everything you have done wrong]

Yahweh is using **I will visit upon you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will punish you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will punish you for]

3.note: Yahweh, through Amos, is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that two people do not travel together unless they have arranged to do so. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Certainly two will not walk together, unless they have agreed!]
The pronoun **they** refers to the two people who agreed to walk together. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [unless the two of them have agreed]

4.q: הֲ⁠יִשְׁאַ֤ג אַרְיֵה֙ בַּ⁠יַּ֔עַר וְ⁠טֶ֖רֶף אֵ֣ין ל֑⁠וֹ
4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that a lion would certainly only roar if it were attacking its prey to catch and eat. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [A lion never roars in the forest when there is no prey for him]

4.q: הֲ⁠יִתֵּ֨ן כְּפִ֤יר קוֹל⁠וֹ֙ מִ⁠מְּעֹ֣נָת֔⁠וֹ בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־לָכָֽד
4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that a young lion growls in its den only when it has caught something. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [A young lion never gives his voice from his den unless he has caught something!]

5.q: הֲ⁠תִפֹּ֤ל צִפּוֹר֙ עַל־פַּ֣ח הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ וּ⁠מוֹקֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין לָ֑⁠הּ
5.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that a bird is caught only when someone has set a trap for it. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [A bird will certainly not fall into a snare on the ground when there is no trap for it!]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that a trap springs up only when it has caught something. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [A snare will certainly not spring up from the ground unless it has something to capture!]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [when it has nothing to capture]

6.q: אִם־יִתָּקַ֤ע שׁוֹפָר֙ בְּ⁠עִ֔יר וְ⁠עָ֖ם לֹ֣א יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ
6.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that people will be afraid when they hear a warning that an enemy is attacking. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Certainly the people will tremble when a shofar is blown in a city!]

Yahweh assumes that readers will know that **a shofar is blown in a city** it is to warn the people of that city that enemies are attacking. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [an alarm is sounded in a city to warn of attacking enemies]

The expression **a shofar is blown** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone blows a shofar]

A **shofar** is a kind of horn that people made from the horn of a ram and blew as a signal. If your readers would not be familiar with what a shofar is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a warning horn]

6.q: תִּהְיֶ֤ה רָעָה֙ בְּ⁠עִ֔יר וַ⁠יהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה
6.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the certainty of the fact that Yahweh can cause disasters to happen as punishment. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [when disaster happens in a city, it is Yahweh who has done it!]

Here and in the next couple of verses, it could be that: (1) Amos is speaking about Yahweh as modeled in the UST (end Yahweh’s quote at the end of verse 2) or (2) Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person throughout these verses. Alternate translation: [and I, Yahweh have not done it]
The pronoun **it** refers to the disaster that happens in the city. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh has not caused that disaster]

7.note: By **Lord Yahweh will not do a thing**, means Yahweh will not bring any judgment to those he has a covenant relationship with, without first telling his prophets who serve him so they can warn the people what will happen if they do not turn from their sinful acts. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [will not bring judgment]

Here and in the next verse, it could be that: (1) Amos is speaking about Yahweh as modeled in the UST (end Yahweh’s quote at the end of verse 2) or (2) Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person throughout these verses. Alternate translation: [I, the Lord Yahweh]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the secret plans that he himself has made. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the secret plans that he has made] or [the secret plans the I have made]

8.note: Yahweh is speaking of the message he’s giving to the people through Amos as if it were the roar of a **lion** that everyone who hears it must fear (see 1:2). Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has roared like a lion]

Yahweh is using the question form to state emphatically that everyone who hears a lion roar will be afraid. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [surely it would make anyone afraid!]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize the fact that when Lord Yahweh has spoken to his prophet, that prophet must proclaim his message. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [surely the one who hears him is compelled to prophesy!]

9.note: The implication is that the messengers are to make this proclamation to the people who live in **the citadels in Ashdod** and in **the citadels in the land of Egypt.** You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Proclaim to the people]

Here, **on the citadels** represents the rulers and other powerful people who live in those citadels. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Tell those who are Ashdod’s rulers and who rule]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and tell them to gather]

The expression **Be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Gather yourselves]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **uproars**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how greatly the people in her midst are rioting]
The pronoun **her** refers to the city of Samaria. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in Samaria]

Yahweh is using the adjective **oppressed** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and the oppressed people within her]

10.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people who live in Samaria. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the inhabitants of Samaria do not know to do right]

Amos, who is conveying Yahweh’s words, is interjecting **the declaration of Yahweh** to emphasize that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **violence** and **destruction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what they have violently and destructively seized]

Here, **violence and destruction** represents the wealth that was attained and stored up as a result of the nation’s acting violently and destructively toward others. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [wealth gained through violence and destruction]

11.note: The word translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [Because they have done these things]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [An adversary will come, and he will be all around the land]

The implication is that **An adversary** is an enemy army that will surround the land and attack its cities. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The army of the adversary will besiege the land on every side]

The pronoun **he** refers to the adversary, and the pronoun **you** refers to the land of Israel around Samaria and the people who live there. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And that adversary will bring down from you Israelites your strength]

Here, **your strength** represents the fortifications that the people of Israel trusted to protect them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And he will bring down your strong defenses]

The expression **be plundered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The adversary would be the one doing this. Alternate translation: [and he will plunder your citadels]

12.q: כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ יַצִּ֨יל הָ⁠רֹעֶ֜ה מִ⁠פִּ֧י הָ⁠אֲרִ֛י שְׁתֵּ֥י כְרָעַ֖יִם א֣וֹ בְדַל־אֹ֑זֶן כֵּ֣ן יִנָּצְל֞וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל
12.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the shepherd** can save only **two legs or a piece of an ear** from a lion that has attacked a sheep, so only a small remnant of the people of Israel will survive. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as the shepherd can recover only parts of a sheep from the mouth of the lion, so only a small remnant of the sons of Israel will be rescued]

The expression **be rescued** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [thus I will only be able to rescue a few of the sons of Israel]

The implication is that these scraps of expensive furniture are all that will be left of the luxury that the people of Samaria now enjoy. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [with only a broken-off side of a bed and a torn piece of a couch left of all their luxury]

Here, **sons** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the sons of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as **Israel.** Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

Scholars are not sure what the word translated as **cover** actually means. It could be: (1) an unknown piece of a couch, as in the UST, or (2) a type of cloth, such as the city of Damascus was known for at a later time. Alternate translation: [and on a damask of a couch] or (3) the word “Damascus,” although spelled a little differently than usual. Alternate translation: [and on a Damascus couch]

13.note: Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Jacob** means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [against the people descended from Jacob]

Amos is interjecting the phrase **the declaration of Yahweh** into what Yahweh is saying to emphasize that what is about to be said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the God who commands the armies of angels. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [God, the commander of the angel armies]

14.note: Yahweh is using the term **in the day** to refer to at a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when the time comes for]

Yahweh is using **my visiting the transgressions of Israel upon him** as a common expression of the culture to mean “my punishing the people of Israel for their transgressions.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my punishing Israel for their transgressions]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **transgressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the wrong things that Israel did]
The pronoun **him** refers to the nation of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [upon that nation]

Yahweh is using **I will also visit upon** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to come against” or “punish.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will also come against]

Here, **the horns of the altar** represents the protection that people superstitiously sought when they took hold of those horns. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the horns of the altar that people grasped for safety will be cut off]

The expression **will be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Yahweh is the one who would do this. Alternate translation: [and I will cut off the horns of the altar]

The top corners of the central altar at Bethel (and others) were shaped like bull horns. These horns were a symbol of the strength of the god that was worshiped there. The horns were considered the most sacred and powerful part of the altar. You could include this information in a footnote if it would be helpful to your readers.
The pronoun **they** refers to the horns of the altar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and those horns will fall to the ground]

15.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the houses of the wealthy people of Israel by naming two extremes, **the winter house** and **the summer house**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all of their many houses]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **houses** that are characterized by decorations of **ivory**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the houses decorated with ivory]

The implication is that these **great houses** are the large and costly homes that wealthy people had built for themselves. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the large, costly houses of the wealthy will come to an end]
See how you translated this same phrase, **the declaration of Yahweh**, in 3:10.
